title: Martha, Mary and Lazarus (29 July)
hookLine: the Bethany family, now celebrated together on one day

cards: There's a guest in the house, and the kitchen is chaos. Bread to bake, water to fetch, a meal to get on the table. One sister is doing all of it.
The other sits on the floor in the next room, listening. The busy one finally comes out, hands still floured, and says it out loud: tell her to help me. The guest is Jesus.
The house is in Bethany, a village near Jerusalem, and the three who live there, two sisters and a brother, are kept together on today's feast.

teach.b: Luke tells the kitchen scene. Martha welcomes Jesus into her house. Mary sits at his feet.

Martha, busy with much serving, asks him to send her sister to help. Jesus answers her gently, saying her name twice. In the Douay-Rheims: "Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about many things."
Careful here means full of cares. He goes on: one thing is necessary, and Mary has chosen the best part. It's easy to hear that as a scolding, and some readers stop there and side with Martha.
But look where the story starts: Martha is the one who opened the door. Without her there's no house, no meal, no place for Mary to sit. Now John's Gospel.
Lazarus, their brother, falls sick, and the sisters send word to Jesus. By the time he comes, Lazarus has been in the tomb for days.

teach.h: SHE GOES OUT TO MEET HIM.
teach.b: And who goes out down the road to meet him? Martha. She tells him straight that if he'd been there, her brother wouldn't have died.
A few lines later, she says she believes he is the Christ, the Son of God. At the tomb, John writes, "Jesus wept." Then he calls Lazarus out.

teach.h: THREE WAYS OF LOVING ONE FRIEND.
teach.b: So the house at Bethany holds three ways of loving the same friend: Martha's work and her bold faith, Mary's listening, and Lazarus, who simply comes back to the table.
The Church keeps all three on one day now. Not the busy one against the quiet one. A household.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus on 29 July, hearing Martha's story from the Gospels of Luke or John at Mass.

o: the sister who served Jesus and met him with faith
a widow who gave her last two coins at the Temple
the mother of James and John, the sons of Zebedee

games.q: the house at Bethany — tap the pairs.

s: Martha only appears in the kitchen scene
in John she goes out to meet Jesus and says she believes he is the Christ.
"Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about many things."
the feast today honors Martha alone
the Church now keeps Martha, Mary and Lazarus together on one day.

games.q: you're Martha. your brother has died, and Jesus has finally arrived, days late. what do you do?
o: stay home and refuse to see him.
go out to meet him on the road.
send Mary to speak for you.
games.why: Martha went out to meet him, told him straight her brother needn't have died, then said she believed he is the Christ.

practice: Think of someone you could welcome, a friend, a neighbor, someone new in town, and picture them at your table.
Notice the Martha in you, already planning the cooking and the cleaning; let that go for a moment and be Mary, just glad they're there, listening.
If you pray, ask God to bless that table; if you don't, simply hold the person in mind.

wordCard.voice: Martha. The sister of Mary and Lazarus in Bethany, who welcomed Jesus into her house, worried over the serving, and went out to meet him with bold faith.

orig.note: Greek: Martha's name as it is written in the Gospels of Luke and John.

carryVoice: Your line: the house at bethany. The work and the listening both belong at that table. See you tomorrow.
